method: Every substantive Markdown note listed in the per-file register received a full-text read. This is distinct from claim-level source verification.

Fact verification focused on important, consequential, version-sensitive, or technically disputable claims. Checks used official standards and documentation, primary literature, source code or locally bounded reproduction as recorded per file.
A no-new-issue status means the selected checks found no new actionable, evidence-backed issue. It does not certify every fact, code sample, equation, or example in that file.

All four COMP90050 weekly notes were read in full; the aggregate was covered by fully reviewing its 169-line diff against the concatenated weekly notes and checking the shared paragraphs. This deduplicated comparison covers the aggregate without treating repeated text as independent claims. The aggregate remains one substantive file.

The supplied audit records were created at different times. Original per-file classifications, checks, evidence links, and limits are retained; current dispositions incorporate the source edits and the final review rather than summing pre-edit status labels.

status_semantics.no-new-issue: Targeted checks did not confirm an actionable correction. It is not an exhaustive correctness certification.
status_semantics.confirmed-error: A source or bounded reproduction contradicts the original statement. Where a correction was applied, the current file record states that disposition.
status_semantics.conditional-clarification: The statement depends on an omitted material version, protocol, host, or usage condition.
status_semantics.source-version-refresh: The cited documentation version changed; the note's original theoretical claim was not found wrong.
status_semantics.unverified: The exact candidate could not be independently confirmed or disproved with available primary evidence and remains explicitly unresolved as a claim.

findings_register.original: Ideal hash function is random, so each bucket will have the same number of records assigned to it irrespective of the actual distribution of search-key values in the file.
findings_register.correction_or_boundary: Good hashing can spread distinct keys approximately evenly; equal keys still hash to the same bucket. Skew/duplicates can produce overflow chains, so uniform record counts and one-I/O lookup aren't guarantees.
findings_register.evidence_summary: PostgreSQL documents uneven hash distributions, overflow pages and poor behavior for highly non-unique values.
findings_register.disposition: Correction applied in the source note and its aggregate duplicate where applicable; final source review passed.

findings_register.original: ### Dekker's algorithm; c1=1; turn=2; wait until c2==0 or turn==1
findings_register.correction_or_boundary: This code is Peterson's two-process algorithm. Mark as pseudocode assuming atomic registers and sequential consistency, not executable C with ordinary shared int; amend misleading algorithm names and no-hardware/efficiency claims.
findings_register.evidence_summary: University algorithm descriptions exactly match flag[i]=true; turn=j; while flag[j]&&turn==j and state SC/atomic-register requirement.
findings_register.disposition: Correction applied in the source note and its aggregate duplicate where applicable; final source review passed.

findings_register.original: If the participant has voted Yes, coordinator instructs participant to commit; if No, instructs participant abort.
findings_register.correction_or_boundary: Coordinator commits all participants only after all required participants vote YES and its global commit decision is durable. Any NO or timeout before a commit decision leads to a global abort, including YES voters. Individual YES is readiness, not a commit decision.
findings_register.evidence_summary: Gray and Lamport transaction commit paper defines global outcome agreement and all participants prepared before committed.
findings_register.disposition: Correction applied in the source note and its aggregate duplicate where applicable; final source review passed.

findings_register.original: Custom Hook guidance said not to include side effects such as state updates in returned functions or values, which contradicted the note’s own returned setState callback example.
findings_register.correction_or_boundary: Clarified that rendering must remain pure, while a custom Hook may return an event handler/callback that updates state or performs a side effect when invoked.
findings_register.evidence_summary: React documents that side effects must not run during render and identifies event handlers as a valid place for user-triggered side effects. The original blanket wording was too broad and inconsistent with the example.
findings_register.disposition: Corrected in this review; official React/Redux/i18next sources are retained in the file record.

findings_register.original: The CHANGE_LANGUAGE Redux reducer called i18n.changeLanguage(action.payload), causing an external/asynchronous side effect during reducer execution.
findings_register.correction_or_boundary: Moved i18n.changeLanguage(languageCode) into the component event handlers before dispatching the plain language action; the reducer now only returns the next Redux state.
findings_register.evidence_summary: Redux requires reducers to depend only on state/action and return state without effects. i18next documents changeLanguage as a Promise-returning language change operation, so it belongs outside the reducer.
findings_register.disposition: Corrected in this review; official React/Redux/i18next sources are retained in the file record.

findings_register.original: 优雅关闭示例对10秒deadline的setTimeout调用unref()，但正文称这个计时器负责让服务器与跟踪任务未settle时仍能触发强制关闭。
findings_register.correction_or_boundary: 移除unref()，保持deadline计时器引用直到触发或清理完成，并说明unref允许事件循环在无其他活动时先退出。
findings_register.evidence_summary: Node.js v26.12.1官方文档说明Timeout默认保持事件循环活动；unref后如果没有其他活动，进程可以在回调执行前退出。Node v24.22.1本地最小复现中，单独的unref定时器在退出前不执行回调；默认引用的对照定时器会执行。
findings_register.disposition: Corrected the timer reference. Targeted Node v24.22.1 reproduction used a resolved serverClosed promise and abort-only trackedWork promise; the 20 ms deadline aborted tracked work, allowing Promise.allSettled() to settle and cleanup to run. The unref version exited 0 with no stdout; the referenced version printed work-cancelled and cleanup-completed. This was not a full HTTP service or failure drill.

findings_register.original: 对EventSource只写“会自动重连”，未提服务端可通过204响应让客户端停止重连。
findings_register.correction_or_boundary: 补充“通常在连接中断后自动重连；服务端可用HTTP 204告知客户端停止重连”，并保留Last-Event-ID和历史重放前提。
findings_register.evidence_summary: WHATWG HTML Server-sent Events说明客户端在连接关闭后会重连，并明确服务端可用204 No Content使其停止重连；带事件ID的续传仍需服务端有可重放历史。
findings_register.disposition: Clarified the EventSource HTTP 204 stop-reconnect behavior from the WHATWG standard.

findings_register.original: OIDC ID Token检查清单把用issuer密钥和注册算法做密码签名校验写成无条件要求。
findings_register.correction_or_boundary: 增加Authorization Code Flow中直接收到Token Endpoint响应这一限定：OIDC Core允许使用经验证的TLS服务器认证来验证issuer以替代签名检查；其他ID Token仍应按规范校验签名和issuer密钥。
findings_register.evidence_summary: OIDC Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2 §3.1.3.7明确列出issuer、audience等验证，并规定直接与Token Endpoint通信收到的ID Token可用TLS服务器验证替代签名检查；该例外只适用于该路径。

findings_register.original: The topic list grouped 'Quadtree (k-d tree)' as if the names described one spatial structure, while the body already described different split structures.
findings_register.correction_or_boundary: Split the list into separate Quadtree and k-d tree entries and added a distinct k-d tree section for the exam example.
findings_register.evidence_summary: Princeton Algorithms materials distinguish multidimensional search structures; the original wording conflated a four-way quadtree partition with a binary k-d split.
findings_register.disposition: Corrected in both the weekly note and aggregate; final review passed.

findings_register.original: OS synchronization primitives were generalized as interruption-based, expensive, independent of process count, despite the following section describing blocking and wakeup behavior.
findings_register.correction_or_boundary: Describe blocking mutexes/semaphores as parking and waking waiters; implementations may use a user-space atomic fast path and call into the kernel only when needed.
findings_register.evidence_summary: The Linux futex interface documents a kernel wait/wake mechanism commonly used to build synchronization primitives, rather than an interrupt on every lock operation.
findings_register.disposition: Corrected in both the weekly note and aggregate; final review passed.

findings_register.original: The overview called spin locks 'most commonly used' without a workload, environment, or source for the prevalence claim.
findings_register.correction_or_boundary: Removed the prevalence claim and described the limited suitability and CPU cost of busy waiting without ranking synchronization mechanisms.
findings_register.evidence_summary: No comparative prevalence statement is retained; the correction avoids replacing an unsupported frequency claim with another one.
findings_register.disposition: Corrected in both the weekly note and aggregate; final review passed.
